outcome: An explicit three-variable counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture (announced 19-20 July 2026, credited by its announcer to Claude Fable 5) falsifies the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra for every n≥3, via the well-known (easy-direction) implication DC_n ⇒ JC_n; the n=1 and n=2 cases remain open. Separately, Alexander Zheglov has an unreviewed preprint (arXiv:2410.06959, last revised Jan 2026) claiming a proof for n=1, which would be a full resolution of the original problem as usually stated but has not been digested by experts or accepted by a journal.

ai.basis_quote: hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx to my close friend akhil for asking about it and my other close friend fable for working during the world cup final

counterexample.object: An explicit polynomial self-map of C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant (−2) that is not injective (three distinct points collide); padding with untouched coordinates x_4,...,x_n extends it to a Jacobian-conjecture counterexample, and hence (via DC_n ⇒ JC_n) a Dixmier-conjecture counterexample, in every dimension n≥3.
counterexample.verified_how: Described by multiple sources as verifiable directly with any computer algebra system; Terence Tao's blog post is an expert digestion confirming the calculations, though a formal peer-reviewed paper had not appeared as of the sources checked.

disputes.summary: Secondary sources disagree on how to attribute the discovery: some (e.g. a commenter on Tao's blog) insist the correct order is 'Levent Alpöge, with Claude Fable 5' rather than crediting the model as primary discoverer, while other write-ups (kingy.ai, kingy.ai-style commentary, and Wikipedia's own phrasing) describe Fable as having 'found the map.' Alpöge's own X post credits Fable for 'working' on the problem without specifying whether the model produced the construction autonomously or under heavy guidance; no prompt log or discovery record is public.

summary: Two things happened to this problem since 26 January 2024. (1) Alexander Zheglov posted arXiv:2410.06959 in October 2024 claiming a proof that the Dixmier conjecture holds for the first Weyl algebra (n=1), and has continued revising it through a fifth version dated January 2026 (extending it from ~25 to 78 pages, still simplifying the final calculation) with no evidence found of journal acceptance or a published expert digestion — this is `claimed`, not `resolved`, and would only settle the n=1 case of the general conjecture in any case. (2) On 19–20 July 2026, mathematician Levent Alpöge announced (casually, on X) an explicit three-variable counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture, crediting Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 with 'working' on the problem alongside co-conspirator Akhil Mathew. Terence Tao's 21 July 2026 blog post digests the construction (an explicit map with constant Jacobian −2 sending three points to one) and confirms the calculations, though Tao also used an AI chatbot himself to check parts of his own digestion. Since the Dixmier conjecture for the n-th Weyl algebra (DC_n) is known (easy direction, pre-2024) to imply the Jacobian conjecture in n variables (JC_n) — established by Tsuchimoto (2005) and Kanel-Belov/Kontsevich (2007) — the falsity of JC_3 immediately falsifies DC_3, and padding with extra untouched variables falsifies DC_n for every n≥3. This is a genuine case-level result within the scope of the bullet as stated ('any endomorphism of a Weyl algebra'): it is a case of the general Dixmier conjecture across all n, and settling it negatively for n≥3 is a change to what a careful person would write about this problem, hence `partial` rather than `open`. The n=1 and n=2 cases remain open (n=1 only via Zheglov's unreviewed claim; n=2 depends on the still-open plane Jacobian conjecture). I coded the July 2026 event as `ai_role: generated` because Alpöge's own words credit Fable with 'working' on the problem in a context (secondary sources uniformly gloss this as Fable having found/produced the construction) that reads as the model producing the mathematical object rather than merely checking or formalizing a human-made one; but the primary quote itself is genuinely ambiguous about division of labor, and no discovery record or prompt log is public, so this is a judgment call flagged in `competing_reading`.
competing_reading: Alpöge's own words ('fable for working during the world cup final') do not unambiguously state that the model produced the counterexample unassisted; it is equally consistent with heavy human guidance (Alpöge and Mathew directing the search, checking candidates, or supplying the key ansatz) with Fable performing computation/search under close supervision, which would make this `assisted` rather than `generated`. No session transcript, prompt log, or authors' technical writeup has been published to settle which. If a future writeup states the humans supplied the construction and Fable merely verified it, the role would be `none`; if it states the humans set up a search framework and Fable's output was the exact witnessed map with essentially no further human mathematical contribution, `generated` is the better reading, which is what I chose.
what_would_settle_it: A discovery record, session transcript, or a written account by Alpöge/Mathew (paper, blog post, or interview) describing precisely what was given to Claude Fable 5 as input and what came back as output — i.e., whether the model was given the problem cold and returned the map, or was guided step-by-step to a human-supplied construction.

corrections.by: hand review directed by a human reviewer (Alex Fogelson), drafted by Claude (claude-opus-5-5); OVERRULES the judging-pass verdict (JUDGE.md, opus), which proposed `resolved`
corrections.why: Reviewed and retained, at the reviewer's direction, ON A STRICT READING of whether the problem was proven. The judging pass read the bullet's 'any endomorphism of a Weyl algebra' as one claim over every n, so a counterexample for n >= 3 would refute it outright. But the Dixmier conjecture as posed by Dixmier, and as usually meant, concerns the first Weyl algebra A_1, and the cases n = 1 and n = 2 remain open (Zheglov's n = 1 proof is unreviewed). A result that leaves the conjecture's central case open is not counted as resolving it. The n >= 3 counterexamples, obtained from the Jacobian counterexample via DC_n => JC_n, stay recorded as a case, `partial`, direction `refuted`. When the judged copies are applied, this row keeps `partial`.
